meaning: A cluster of SageMaker-managed instances that stays up between jobs. AWS checks its health and repairs it, and Slurm or Amazon EKS schedules the jobs on it.
A pretrained network that takes camera images and an instruction and outputs robot actions.
Fine-tuning a pretrained VLA on demonstrations recorded with your own robot.
The batch scheduler of classic supercomputing. Users submit shell scripts to it, and Slurm runs them on the nodes of a queue.
The Slurm command that submits a job script to a queue.
The Slurm command that launches one step of a job on the allocated nodes. HyperPod adds the --auto-resume=1 flag to it.
Slurm's name for a queue and the set of nodes that serve it.
AWS's managed Kubernetes service, which runs the Kubernetes control plane for you. A HyperPod cluster supplies its worker nodes, and the two clusters are mapped one to one.
HyperPod's unit of capacity: a named set of instances of one type, or of a flexible list of types, with a count and one purchase option.
An instance group that lists up to 20 instance types in priority order. HyperPod moves down the list when capacity for a type is missing.
A prepaid SageMaker GPU reservation with a start and an end date, attached to one instance group.
HyperPod's default way of filling instance groups. It records a target count, retries failed launches in the background and lets jobs start on the capacity that has already arrived.
A set-up script that HyperPod runs once on each new node.
A Kubernetes package. HyperPod's chart installs its health monitoring agent, device plug-ins and training operators on the EKS cluster.
The Kubernetes controller that turns a training job description, such as a PyTorchJob, into pods.
A standard library interface for sending messages between the processes of a parallel program. HyperPod's Helm chart installs the Kubeflow MPI operator for jobs that use it.
The Kubeflow Training Operator's object that describes one PyTorch training run.
The HyperPod training operator's job object. Its runPolicy holds a retry count and log rules that detect a hung job.
The EC2 network device through which the nodes of one multi-node training job exchange data.
NVIDIA's GPU diagnostic tool. Running it at its most thorough level is the longest part of a deep health check.
An optional stress test that HyperPod runs on a new or replaced instance before work lands on it.
The HyperPod process on each node that watches for hardware faults and labels the node's health.
The cluster setting that lets HyperPod reboot or replace a faulty node without anyone asking it to.
The mechanism that restarts a job after its node was replaced. On Kubernetes it is two annotations on the job; on Slurm it is a flag on a job step.
An open-source Kubernetes node autoscaler. It launches nodes for pods that cannot be scheduled and removes empty nodes. On the EKS path, HyperPod runs it for you.
The object that lists which instance groups Karpenter may scale.
Karpenter's object that points at a node class and holds the rules for removing nodes.
The NodePool setting for how long Karpenter waits before it removes a node it no longer needs.
HyperPod's add-on for sharing an EKS-orchestrated cluster between teams. It installs Kueue and adds a cluster policy and a compute allocation for each team.
A Kubernetes controller that holds a job until quota is free and then admits it.
Kueue's queue for one namespace. A team's jobs name it in a label.
The single task governance object for a cluster. It holds the priority classes and the rule for sharing idle compute.
One team's quota: its resources, a sharing strategy, a borrow limit and a preemption rule.
How much idle quota a team may use beyond its own allocation, as a percentage of that allocation.
Stopping a running task so that a higher-priority task, or the team that lent the quota, can use the compute.
A Kubernetes mark on a node that stops new pods from being scheduled there.
The time Kubernetes gives a pod to stop after it is told to. A training script can write a last checkpoint during that time.
A managed parallel file system that every node mounts. Here it holds datasets and checkpoints.
A HyperPod feature that recovers a failed node's training state from healthy peers.
A HyperPod feature that writes checkpoints to node memory, copies them to adjacent nodes and saves them periodically to storage.
A HyperPod feature that grows and shrinks a training job by saving a checkpoint and resuming with a different number of workers.
